title: Shooting Relay Race
description: Two teams race to score a set number of baskets in a relay, adding fun competition and pressure to shooting practice and rewarding smart, controlled shots.

content.objective: Shoot with good technique under light time pressure, work as a team and cheer each other on without rushing.
content.setup: Two teams line up on either side of half court. Each team has a ball. A cone marks the shooting spot on each side of the free-throw line.
instructions: The first player on each team dribbles to the shooting cone, shoots once and rebounds their own shot.
If the shot is missed, keep shooting until it is made, then dribble back and pass the ball to the next player.
The first team to score a set number of baskets (e.g. 10) wins the round.
Change the shooting spot for every round: free-throw line, wing, block, then short corner.
Losing teams do a simple team task, such as ten line-jumps, and rejoin.
coachingPoints: Shoot with balanced feet and a full follow-through even under pressure.
Speed comes from quick footwork, not from rushing the shot.
Rebound your own shot and pass with a bounce to the next player.
commonMistakes: Rushing the shot with poor balance.
Long, high-arc passes that slow the relay.
content.safety: Teams stand on opposite sides of the key to avoid collisions and wait clear of the rebound area.
progressions: Require a pass and catch-and-shoot on the move for every attempt.
regressions: Reduce the distance and use a lower target such as five baskets.
variations: Alternate right-hand and left-hand layups before the shot.
